title: Excel: Copilot Agent Mode (Edit with Copilot) for Microsoft 365 users without a Copilot licence
summary: Hold: the briefing treats protection of labelled workbooks as an open question, although Microsoft documents that the Copilot DLP policy covers open Excel files. Its default-state rating also conflates availability with user-initiated workbook editing. The listed policy path, registry setting and licence-assignment command are supported.

claims.claim: The service description lists Edit with Copilot as a Premium feature requiring a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Edit with Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote [footnote 2]. Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) features: A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is required to access this feature.

Cite https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/frequently-asked-questions-about-copilot-in-excel. claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an add-on plan with licensing prerequisites.

claims.claim: The feature is included for subscribers without the Copilot add-on, with the conflicting service-description requirement noted.

claims.fix: Keep licensing.model as included and add the FAQ's eligible entitlement to licensing.notes: 'The Excel FAQ lists a Copilot Chat-eligible Microsoft 365 or Office 365 business or enterprise subscription for standard access without the add-on.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/frequently-asked-questions-about-copilot-in-excel and retain the attributed service-description conflict.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default is rated on even though the briefing describes a capability users choose to invoke and says users who never open Copilot notice nothing.
claims.quote: defaultState: "on"; impact: "users who never open the Copilot pane notice nothing". The standard defines user-opt-in as "available, but each user or maker chooses to turn it on or to use it".
claims.fix: Set defaultState to user-opt-in. Replace 'it arrives with no admin action' in Why it matters with 'users initiate workbook edits by submitting a request to Copilot'. https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/get-started-with-copilot-in-excel says editing follows a submitted prompt; its default edit mode does not mean unattended workbook changes.

claims.claim: Neither this roadmap record nor the March release-notes entry describes a required administrator enablement step.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edit with Copilot Excel admin action', '543242 default'. Read the roadmap and March 10 release-notes entry; their steps describe opening Copilot and submitting a request, not administrator enablement.

claims.claim: The feature description does not specify a new sign-in, permission or connector requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Excel Agent Mode sign in permissions'. Read the roadmap, March release notes, Excel get-started page and Excel FAQ. They describe existing subscription, privacy and tenant requirements, not a new Agent Mode sign-in or connector.

claims.where: controls[2]; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant UI or API setting is documented that independently turns Agent Mode in Excel on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edit with Copilot Excel policy', 'Excel Agent Mode disable Graph', 'Edit with Copilot Excel Microsoft Graph settings'. Read overview, Manage Copilot Chat and Excel FAQ; FAQ says Copilot in Excel can't be turned off independently.
claims.fix: Keep both null sides. Replace the row note with: 'The Excel FAQ says Copilot in Excel is a Microsoft Copilot Chat tool, cannot be turned off independently, and all admin settings controlling Copilot Chat access apply.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/frequently-asked-questions-about-copilot-in-excel.

claims.claim: Whether the Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat DLP location prevents processing labelled workbooks in this Excel experience remains undocumented.
claims.quote: When a file is open in Word, Excel, or PowerPoint and has a sensitivity label for which DLP policy is configured to prevent processing by Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat, the skills in these apps are disabled.
claims.fix: Remove this open question, or replace it with: 'Microsoft documents that Copilot DLP can prevent processing sensitivity-labelled files open in Excel. The policy is evaluated at file open; a label applied mid-session is enforced when the file is next opened.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about. The Excel FAQ identifies this experience as a Copilot Chat tool; do not retain an unlicensed-user applicability gap.
